clue.text: Traffic force includes thousands

indicators.note: includes says the word for force holds the other piece within it

parts.note: to force someone is to coerce them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them stand for thousands

explanation.surface: A police force has thousands of officers dealing with road traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in the sense of trade or dealing in goods is a synonym.

clue.text: Two companies combine on a silk product

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company
the second CO for company

explanation.surface: Two firms merge to make silk goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A silkworm spins a casing of silk thread around itself, which is where raw silk comes from.

clue.text: Teacher with set of answers needed for Common Entrance

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
a key lists the answers to a test or puzzle

explanation.surface: A teacher has the answer sheet ready for the Common Entrance exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Common Entrance is an English exam for entry to private schools; here it means a door everyone shares, which one key opens alongside many others.
explanation.definitionFit: One key that opens every lock in a building is what a shared doorway needs.

clue.text: No longer lie about being an outcast

parts.note: EX means former, no longer so

indicators.note: about signals the letters of lie are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped lying finds themselves shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LIE into ILE; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A banished person living away from their homeland is a social outcast.

clue.text: It gives lift when flier has to go over an obstacle

indicators.note: in a down answer the bird's name sits above the other piece

parts.note: a crow is a bird, a flier
a bar is a barrier or obstacle

explanation.surface: A bird must fly over a barrier to get any lift.
explanation.definitionFit: This iron lever is used to prise and raise heavy things.

clue.text: Cigar left perhaps-it's very pungent

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged differently, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A cigar left lying about gives off a strong smell.
explanation.definitionFit: This bulb used in cooking has a famously strong smell and taste.

clue.text: The irresolute chairman's lack of control

indicators.note: irresolute means wavering and unsettled, so the letters do not stay put

parts.note: the letters of the word as printed, with its S

explanation.surface: An indecisive chairman's failure to keep order in the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A state without government or authority is a lack of control.

clue.text: Girl given ring might be thrown over by cowboy

definitions.text: might be thrown over by cowboy

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A girl given an engagement ring might be thrown over by her cowboy boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown over' looks like jilting but means the rope tossed over cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope noose is what a ranch hand tosses over a steer.

clue.text: Understood to have won popularity

explanation.surface: Understood how to become popular.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both grasped an idea and became fashionable.

clue.text: Sort of alibi that cannot be forged

explanation.surface: An alibi so solid it cannot be faked.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbreakable alibi is called this, and the brittle metal of that name cannot be hammered into shape.

clue.text: As a sun resort it's capital

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: As a sunny resort, it is a top place to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but signals the letters are re-sorted; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Some mundane chores are repetitive

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some everyday household chores are tediously repetitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated sounds or reflections repeat what went before.

clue.text: Look after a bull for Daisy

indicators.note: after places the word for look behind the animal

parts.note: an ox is a bull or bovine
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a bull named Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as caring for an animal, and Daisy looks like the bull's name; Daisy is in fact a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild flower is a type of large white field daisy.

clue.text: Setting for new clock in the City?

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the city's name

parts.note: Bath is an English city

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The scene for a new clock being installed in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLOCK as CKCLO. 'the City' usually means London's financial district; here it is Bath, a city in the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted backdrop on stage forms the scene's setting.

clue.text: Pin inserted into a joint

explanation.surface: A pin pushed into a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spike is a pin, and it is pushed through a joint of meat for roasting.

clue.text: Mysteries of the variable south wind?

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: Puzzles about an unpredictable southerly breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' rearranges the nine letters of SOUTH WIND; 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Detective stories in which the reader guesses the culprit are mysteries.

clue.text: Gold coin replacing old S. American currency

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: replacing read as re-placing, putting in new positions, signals the letters are moved

explanation.surface: A gold coin taking the place of an outdated South American money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' re-places COIN as INOC. 'currency' means a current, so the definition describes a South American river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current, and this one flows through Venezuela.

clue.text: Telephoning, hung up

explanation.surface: Making a call, then putting the receiver down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means connected on a phone call, and also pegged out to dry like laundry.

clue.text: Neglect nothing on a job

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a mission is a task or job

explanation.surface: Neglecting to do anything while on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure to do something is neglect.

clue.text: Centre of a dance revolution

parts.note: reads like the start of a dance craze, but describes the pole that springtime dancers circle round

explanation.surface: The heart of a dance-floor revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers weave ribbons around this tall post, which stands at the middle as they go round.

clue.text: Dash from France

parts.note: reads like a run from France but means flair, a word borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A quick escape from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Style and vigour, a flair that English took from French.

clue.text: Hostility is here yet I'm resolved about one point

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the compass point
resolved, read as re-solved, has the letters worked out again in a new order

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: There is hostility here, yet I am determined on one matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' makes EMITY from YET I'M, which goes 'about' N; 'is here' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will and antagonism are hostility.

clue.text: It takes pluck to remove it

definitions.text: It takes pluck to remove it

parts.words: It takes pluck to remove it
parts.note: reads as needing courage, but means tweezing hairs from above the eye

explanation.surface: Removing it takes courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairs on the brow ridge are thinned with tweezers, pulled out one by one.

clue.text: Is against using Latin

parts.note: reads like opposing the language, but asks for the Latin word for against

explanation.surface: Someone objects to using Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word meaning against, used in legal case names and fixtures.

clue.text: Fan fire?

explanation.surface: A fan of fire, or a stoker.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan a flame or fire someone up is to rouse or excite.

clue.text: I had been in front, but became lazy

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
led means was in the lead, in front

explanation.surface: Once the leader, a runner slacked off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazed about doing nothing, loafed.

clue.text: A bit part

explanation.surface: A small acting role.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a bit or a part of something.

clue.text: Dotty sort of dance?

parts.note: dotty looks like crazy but points to a dotted fabric pattern that shares its name with a lively dance

explanation.surface: A mad kind of dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bohemian dance in two-time, also the name of a spotted pattern.

clue.text: Like marquetry of fashionable Dali design

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: design indicates the letters are arranged in a new pattern

explanation.surface: Like marquetry in a trendy design by Salvador Dalí.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is wood veneer set into a surface, so it is set in.

clue.text: Girls maybe right to accept glamorous underwear

indicators.note: to accept means the word for girls takes in the other letter

parts.note: fillies are young female horses, slang for girls

explanation.surface: Girls might be happy to accept glamorous lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacy, flouncy lingerie is glamorous underwear.

clue.text: Dim sun, when out, hardly encourages it

definitions.text: Dim sun, when out, hardly encourages it

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A weak sun does little to encourage stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DIM SUN; the whole clue also says a pale sun discourages going without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Going naked outdoors is what weak sunshine discourages.

clue.text: Those that feel the heat for those who feel the cold

definitions.text: for those who feel the cold

explanation.surface: People who perspire, and garments for the chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: People who perspire in heat, and woollen jumpers worn when cold.
